feedback: Written before this candidate races, so no outcome is claimed for it. The evidence is iteration 1 (score 134.06, the best so far). The oval finished in 1 of 20 trials at a mean finish time of 1.65 s, so base_speed 1.4 is already fast enough to finish with time to spare. The s-bend and slalom ended 100% off track, with 1.15 to 1.25 line-loss events per run and steering_oscillation of 0.18 to 0.29. The candidate's own rationale says the array and sensor footprint move, which is the right direction for line loss. The problem is that it also cuts base_speed from 1.4 to 1.1. Iteration 1 shows that 1.4 was not too fast, and 1.1 gives the 3 s limit little margin: a 300-step run needs roughly 1.5 m/s on average to finish. A reduction to 1.1 would likely cost the 500-point completion bonus even if line loss improves. The change to kp (3.0 to 3.5) combined with a wider array is also a simultaneous change to two terms, so the next race cannot tell which one helped. Keep base_speed at 1.4 so the speed effect is held constant. Keep the sensor widening to x = ±0.036 and sensor_size 0.016, and keep kd at 0.4 and ki at 0.02. Make the kp change in one step. After the race, judge the array change by line_loss_events and max_error on the s-bend and slalom, and by whether any off-track exit still happens at a bend. If line_loss_events are still above 0.5 per run, raise kp further (toward 4.0) or kd (toward 0.6) to address turn-in lag. If the robot stays on the line but progress stalls below 0.6 with no off-track exit, then base_speed is the limit and the next step is to raise it in 0.1 steps from 1.4 rather than to lower it.
requested_changes: Keep base_speed at 1.4, the value that gave the one oval finish in iteration 1 at 1.65 s. Lowering it to 1.1 risks failing the 3 s limit and losing the 500-point completion bonus.

Keep the wider array (sensor x at ±0.036 m with sensor_size 0.016) and kp 3.5, but hold kd at 0.4 and ki at 0.02 so the race separates the array and gain effects from speed. Iteration 1 line-loss events of 1.15 to 1.45 per run were the main failure.
If line_loss_events are still above 0.5 per run after this change, raise kd from 0.4 toward 0.6 before raising kp further, since iteration 1 steering_oscillation was already 0.29 on the oval.
